methodologyNotes: Covers 14 adult performance tennis racquets ("player's" and "tweener" frames, 97-100 sq in head sizes) that a 2026 buyer commonly cross-shops, spanning the current flagship lines from Babolat, Wilson, Head, Yonex, Tecnifibre, Prince, and Dunlop. Excludes junior, recreational/oversize (105+ sq in), pickleball-crossover, and pro-stock/tour-only frames. All specs are the manufacturer-published figures as listed on the frame's primary US retail spec sheet (overwhelmingly Tennis Warehouse, the industry-standard US stringing/retail reference that reproduces brand spec sheets verbatim), cross-checked against the brand's own site or an independent US retailer where noted. strung_weight_oz is the manufacturer's strung weight for a no-overgrip, no-dampener frame (unstrung weight is usually ~15-20g lower and is not separately tracked). balance_point_mm is the strung balance point converted from the published inches figure (in x 25.4, rounded to the nearest mm); all 14 frames are head-light. string_pattern is written 'mains x crosses'. beam_width_mm is written 'tip/throat/shaft' in mm as published (a single number means a uniform/constant beam). stiffness_ra is the manufacturer's RA flex rating (unitless, lower = more flexible). grip_size lists the full range of grip sizes sold for that exact SKU, in US inches with the L1-L8 index, e.g. '4 1/8"-4 1/2" (L1-L4)' — some current SKUs (VCORE 100 8th Gen, Percept 97, the Pro Staff 97 v14 Session Soiree cosmetic) ship in only 3 grip sizes rather than the usual 4, per the retailer's own size selector. racket_length_in is standard length (27 in) for every model in this set. swingweight is the manufacturer's stock strung swingweight. priceUsd is the US MSRP for the frame's standard/base colorway and string pattern (unstrung, i.e. as a bare frame) at the time of access; where a model is sold in the US only through a special cosmetic (e.g. Wilson Pro Staff 97 v14, currently listed stateside as the 'Session Soiree' Roland Garros colorway) the price and grip range are taken from that active listing, which retailers state carries identical specs to the standard frame. The Tecnifibre TF-X1 300 has no confirmed current US MSRP (only a marked-down sale price and a EUR price were found), so priceUsd is null per the null-over-guess rule. accessedAt reflects the date all live pages were fetched for this dataset.

The downloaded product photo was visually confirmed to show a grey/yellow 'AERO' cosmetic frame matching this generation.
